replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Yes, sometimes I do feel anxious when faced with math problems. It’s not just the difficulty, but the fear of not understanding or making mistakes. I avoid it when I can, which is why I’ve never really pushed myself to explore it further, even though I know it’s important for some careers.

Honestly, I’m not sure I’d trust them enough to help me, especially since math already feels so confusing. I prefer asking friends or looking up simple explanations online instead.

It’s easier said than done, though!

I’ve never actually done this, but I think you start by finding the derivative of the function, f'(x). Then, you set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x to find critical points. replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: I’ve never heard of Principal Component Analysis, so I couldn’t explain it even if I tried! It sounds like something way beyond what I’ve learned. For someone like me, who struggles with math, tools like that might actually make it feel less scary and more fun to learn.
